prompt: Which U.S. president signed the Civil Rights Act of 1964 into law?
factBlurb: Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act on July 2, 1964, reportedly telling an aide afterward, 'We have lost the South for a generation.'

prompt: Which spice is the inner bark of a cinnamon tree, which naturally curls into quills as it dries?
factBlurb: True cinnamon (Ceylon cinnamon) is thinner and more delicate than the more common cassia, which is thicker and stronger.

prompt: How many times has France won the FIFA World Cup?
factBlurb: France has won the World Cup three times: in 1998 (at home), 2018, and 2022.

prompt: Which country pioneered the concept of rehabilitation-focused prisons in the 1980s?
factBlurb: Norway developed a rehabilitation-focused prison model that emphasizes restorative justice and has one of the world's lowest recidivism rates.

prompt: The Bugatti Veyron's engine has how many cylinders?
factBlurb: The Veyron's W16 engine is essentially two narrow-angle V8s fused together — 16 cylinders, four turbochargers, and 1,001 horsepower when it launched in 2005.

prompt: Which rapper born Clifford Joseph Harris Jr. goes by a two-letter stage name?
factBlurb: T.I. originally went by 'Tip' (a childhood nickname) and later shortened it to 'T.I.' when he discovered another rapper already had the name Tip.

prompt: What is the name of the famous guitar solo in Lynyrd Skynyrd's 'Free Bird'?
options: There is no single named solo — it has three guitarists trading off
factBlurb: Free Bird's extended outro features Allen Collins, Gary Rossington, and Ed King trading guitar lines — no single named solo, just three southern rockers cutting loose.

prompt: Which European country has a centuries-old tradition of producing butter wrapped in linen and stored in bogs for preservation?
factBlurb: Irish bog butter, preserved in anaerobic peat bogs for centuries, was recently found during excavations — the cold, airless environment kept it edible.

prompt: Which TV movie dramatized the real-life scandal of a Texas mom who plotted to kill a rival cheerleader's mother?
options: The Positively True Adventures of the Alleged Texas Cheerleader-Murdering Mom
Fab Five: The Texas Cheerleader Scandal
factBlurb: The 1993 HBO film starred Holly Hunter and was based on the true story of Wanda Holloway, who hired a hitman to eliminate her daughter's cheerleading competition.

prompt: In the 1980s, which Japanese automaker colluded with Toyota on a secret joint venture that produced the Toyota Corolla's twin — the Geo Prizm?
factBlurb: NUMMI — New United Motor Manufacturing Inc. — was a secret 1984 joint factory in Fremont, CA where GM and Toyota built nearly identical cars side by side.

prompt: In snooker, which color ball is worth the most points when potted?
factBlurb: The black ball is worth 7 points — the highest of the six colored balls, which is why it's the prize pot in a maximum 147 break.

prompt: What is the name of the rail technology where the train is suspended and propelled by magnetic forces, with no wheels touching the track?
factBlurb: Maglev — short for magnetic levitation — uses powerful electromagnets to lift and propel the train, eliminating friction and allowing speeds above 370 mph.

prompt: In 'The Incredibles,' what is Mr. Incredible's real last name?
factBlurb: Bob Parr — a deliberately ordinary surname — reflects the family's forced life of suburban anonymity after superheroes are outlawed.

prompt: Which Pope was the first to take the name 'Francis'?
factBlurb: Jorge Mario Bergoglio, elected in 2013, was the first pope ever to choose the name Francis — honoring St. Francis of Assisi.

prompt: Mount Elbrus, the highest peak in Europe, is located in which mountain range?
factBlurb: Mount Elbrus at 18,510 feet sits in the Caucasus range in Russia and is considered the highest point in Europe by most geographers.

prompt: In the TV series 'Supernatural,' what is the name of the yellow-eyed demon who killed Sam and Dean Winchester's mother?
factBlurb: Azazel, nicknamed 'Yellow Eyes,' kick-started the entire series by killing Mary Winchester on the ceiling of Sam's nursery in 1983.

prompt: The idiom 'where there's smoke, there's fire' is a proverb meaning what?
options: Danger is always visible before it strikes
Rumors usually have some basis in truth
Small problems always become large ones
Evidence can be fabricated to mislead
factBlurb: The proverb dates back at least to ancient Rome — Plautus wrote a version of it around 200 BC, making it one of the oldest surviving Western proverbs.

prompt: Which steak cut is sourced from the spinalis dorsi muscle — the cap that sits on top of the ribeye — and is considered by many butchers to be the most flavorful single bite on the cow?
factBlurb: The spinalis dorsi, or ribeye cap, combines extreme marbling with a tender texture — it's the prized outer ring you sometimes see cut away and sold separately at high-end butchers.

prompt: Which rapper released 'The Chronic' in 1992?
factBlurb: Dr. Dre's solo debut that defined G-funk and introduced Snoop Dogg to the world.

prompt: What is the traditional liquid base of a classic French onion soup?
factBlurb: Slow-caramelized onions simmered in rich beef stock — topped with a crouton and melted Gruyère — give French onion soup its deep, savory sweetness.

prompt: The genus Nematostella (the starlet sea anemone) is widely used in science because it is a model organism for studying what?
factBlurb: Nematostella sits near the base of the animal family tree and shares many genes with humans, making it invaluable for studying how complex body plans first evolved.

prompt: What is the name of the active volcano on Ross Island, Antarctica, that has a persistent lava lake in its crater?
factBlurb: Mount Erebus is the world's southernmost active volcano and one of only a handful on Earth with a long-lived convecting lava lake.

prompt: Saint Maximilian Kolbe, who volunteered to die in place of a stranger at Auschwitz, was a priest from which country?
factBlurb: Polish Franciscan friar Maximilian Kolbe offered himself to be starved to death in place of a fellow prisoner at Auschwitz in 1941; he was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 1982.

prompt: Which one-hit wonder band asked "Who Let the Dogs Out" in 2000?
factBlurb: "Who Let the Dogs Out" won a Grammy for Best Dance Recording in 2001, despite being widely mocked by critics.

prompt: Which work boot company, founded in 1917 in New England, is known for its 'Bean Boot' heritage line?
factBlurb: L.L.Bean's iconic Maine Hunting Shoe, launched in 1912, became the template for modern work and outdoor boots.

prompt: The asteroid belt sits between the orbits of which two planets?
factBlurb: The asteroid belt contains millions of rocky objects but is so spread out that spacecraft pass through it with ease.

prompt: Which company created the Game Boy handheld console?
factBlurb: Nintendo's Game Boy, designed by Gunpei Yokoi and launched in 1989, sold over 118 million units including the Game Boy Color.

prompt: The skin of a ripe Canary melon has a texture often described as which of the following?
factBlurb: Unlike the netted skin of a cantaloupe, the Canary melon has a smooth, waxy, bright-yellow rind that almost looks lacquered.

prompt: Which skateboard deck company was founded by George Powell and is known for technical innovation?
factBlurb: George Powell founded his company to push the technical limits of skateboard design and manufacturing precision.

prompt: Which toxin, also found in puffer fish, is produced by some newt species as a defense?
factBlurb: Rough-skinned newts produce tetrodotoxin — the same nerve-blocking poison in puffer fish — making them one of the most toxic animals in North America.

prompt: The iconic 'Burnside Project' skate park was built illegally under a bridge in which U.S. city?
factBlurb: Skaters started pouring concrete under Portland's Burnside Bridge in 1990 without permission — the city eventually embraced it, and it's now a protected landmark.

prompt: What is the name of the symbiote alien that bonds with Peter Parker to create a black suit?
factBlurb: The Venom symbiote first bonded with Spider-Man in Secret Wars (1984), giving him a sleek black suit — before moving on to Eddie Brock.

prompt: Which Catholic feast day, celebrated on January 6th, commemorates the visit of the Magi to the infant Jesus?
factBlurb: Epiphany — from the Greek for 'manifestation' — marks the Magi's arrival and is considered the official end of the Christmas season in many Catholic traditions.

prompt: The 'Doll's Eyes' plant (Actaea pachypoda) is named for its berries, which look like what?
options: Small glass marbles with black pupils
Pale blue spheres with dark veins
Ivory beads strung on black wire
factBlurb: Doll's Eyes berries are white with a black dot — exactly like a doll's glass eye — mounted on vivid red stalks, making the plant look genuinely unsettling and it is fatally toxic.

prompt: The Millau Viaduct, one of the world's tallest bridges, is located in which country?
factBlurb: France's Millau Viaduct, opened in 2004, has a mast that soars higher than the Eiffel Tower — it crosses the Tarn River gorge in the south of France.

prompt: Homecoming is traditionally associated with which sport's season?
factBlurb: Homecoming games are almost always football games — the tradition started as a way to bring alumni back to campus for the biggest home game of the fall season.

prompt: Which U.S. state produces the most pumpkins by weight?
factBlurb: Illinois grows roughly 80–90% of the pumpkins processed for canned goods in the U.S., centered around Morton, which calls itself the 'Pumpkin Capital of the World.'

prompt: Which classic rock band was originally called 'The New Yardbirds' before changing their name?
factBlurb: Jimmy Page formed The New Yardbirds in 1968 to fulfill Scandinavian tour dates, then renamed them Led Zeppelin before recording their debut album.

prompt: In the film Patch Adams, Williams plays a medical student who believes what is essential to healing?
factBlurb: Patch Adams (1998) showcased Williams' belief that humor and compassion are vital to medicine.

prompt: Which U.S. state capital is the highest in elevation?
factBlurb: Santa Fe, New Mexico sits at 7,000 feet above sea level, making it the highest state capital in the continental U.S.

prompt: In what year did SpaceX's Falcon 9 first successfully land a first-stage booster for reuse?
factBlurb: On December 21, 2015, Falcon 9 became the first orbital-class rocket to land its first stage vertically, revolutionizing spaceflight economics.

prompt: What is the name of the clown mascot of McDonald's?
factBlurb: Ronald McDonald debuted in 1963, played by future Washington Redskins mascot Willard Scott in the first TV commercials.

prompt: Which actress, later the star of a massive HBO series, appeared in a Clearasil acne cream commercial in the late 1980s?
factBlurb: Sarah Michelle Gellar got her start in commercials — including Clearasil — before 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer' made her the queen of '90s TV.

prompt: What is the name of the tiny, nearly invisible jellyfish responsible for 'sea lice' stings on swimmers in the Gulf of Mexico?
factBlurb: Thimble jellyfish larvae are so small they pass through swimwear fabric, causing a rash of stinging welts — what beachgoers call 'sea lice' — along the Gulf Coast each summer.

prompt: Which electrolyte do sports drinks like Gatorade primarily use to trigger thirst and encourage continued drinking?
factBlurb: Sodium is the key thirst-triggering electrolyte — it's why sports drinks are slightly salty and why you keep wanting more.

prompt: What is the real name of the superhero Captain America?
factBlurb: Steve Rogers was a scrawny kid from Brooklyn who became the world's first super-soldier after receiving the experimental Super-Soldier Serum.

prompt: Which legislation, passed in 1938, established the 40-hour workweek and federal minimum wage in the United States?
factBlurb: The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 set a federal minimum wage of 25 cents per hour and capped the standard workweek at 40 hours — a landmark win for American workers.

prompt: Before Ditka was hired to coach the Bears in 1982, he had never been a head coach at any level. Who hired him?
factBlurb: Bears founder George Halas personally handpicked Ditka, calling him 'my kind of guy' — it was one of Halas's last major decisions before his death in 1983.

prompt: Which team do the Chicago Bears play their home games for in the NFL?
factBlurb: The Bears have been in the NFC North (formerly the NFC Central) since the NFL's 1970 AFL-NFL merger.

prompt: What is the maximum number of substitutions allowed per team in a World Cup match?
factBlurb: Starting in 2022, teams are allowed five substitutions per match in the World Cup, up from the traditional three.

prompt: The American Robin is the state bird of which U.S. state?
factBlurb: Michigan, Wisconsin, and Connecticut all claim the American Robin — making it one of the most shared state birds in the country.

prompt: The Brazil nut, a trail mix staple, is unique because it cannot be commercially farmed in plantations. Why?
options: Its roots release toxins that kill neighboring trees
It only grows above 10,000 feet elevation
It requires old-growth forest bees for pollination
Its seeds only germinate after a wildfire
factBlurb: Brazil nuts depend on a specific orchid bee found only in intact Amazon rainforest to pollinate their flowers — remove the old-growth forest and the trees simply stop producing nuts.

prompt: In which country were fireworks invented?
factBlurb: Chinese alchemists accidentally discovered gunpowder around 800 AD, and fireworks followed soon after.

prompt: Which of these is NOT a common environmental condition that promotes black mold growth?
factBlurb: Black mold thrives in warm, moist environments; cold temperatures actually slow its growth significantly.

prompt: The carambola fruit is nicknamed the 'starfruit' because of the shape it forms when sliced. How many points does that star have?
factBlurb: Carambola's five ridges running the length of the fruit produce a perfect five-pointed star cross-section — making it one of the most photogenic fruits in the world.

prompt: What is the name of the ice cream bar that Unilever's Good Humor brand introduced in 1920 — one of the first individually wrapped ice cream bars on a stick?
factBlurb: Harry Burt Sr. created the Good Humor Bar in 1920 in Youngstown, Ohio, coating vanilla ice cream in chocolate and adding a wooden stick so it wouldn't drip on your hands.

prompt: Which of these animals can sting using a structure called a nematocyst?
factBlurb: Sea anemones fire microscopic harpoon-like nematocysts — the same stinging cells used by jellyfish and coral — to paralyze prey.

prompt: In what decade did diesel cars become popular in Europe?
factBlurb: European diesel adoption accelerated in the 1990s when fuel taxes and emissions regulations favored the efficiency and low CO₂ of diesel cars.

prompt: Which vaccine, developed in the 1790s, is considered the world's first vaccine ever created?
factBlurb: Edward Jenner used cowpox to protect against smallpox in 1796 — kicking off the entire science of vaccination.

prompt: What does the 'I' term in a PID controller correct for?
factBlurb: The Integral term sums up past errors — it eliminates the persistent offset that a Proportional-only controller leaves behind, pushing the process all the way to the setpoint.

prompt: The Leatherman multi-tool was invented in which decade?
factBlurb: Tim Leatherman invented his first multi-tool in 1980 after a frustrating trip through Europe with a faulty car and a simple pocketknife.

prompt: Which female artist released the album 'Daydream Nation' in 1989, making her a major influence on 90s music?
factBlurb: Sonic Youth's 'Daydream Nation' came out in 1988 and became a touchstone for 90s alternative rock.

prompt: In 'Midnight Run,' Robert De Niro's bounty hunter Jack Walsh and his fugitive bond-jumper spend time in a bar in the American Southwest. What is the profession of the fugitive, Jonathan Mardukas?
factBlurb: Mardukas is a mob accountant who embezzled $15 million from a crime boss and donated it to charity — earning him the nickname 'The Duke.'

prompt: Which bridge held the record as the world's longest suspension bridge for over 25 years after opening in 1998?
factBlurb: Japan's Akashi Kaikyō Bridge has a main span of 1,991 meters — it survived a magnitude 7.2 earthquake during construction.

prompt: In what year did the Panama Canal open to traffic?
factBlurb: The canal opened on August 15, 1914, cutting the sea route between the Atlantic and Pacific by nearly 8,000 miles.

prompt: In three-cushion billiards, what must the cue ball do before contacting the second object ball to score a point?
factBlurb: Three-cushion billiards requires the cue ball to contact at least three rail cushions before or after hitting the first object ball, then strike the second — no pockets involved.

prompt: Which country's prison system was used as a model for Australia's colonial penal colonies?
factBlurb: Britain established penal colonies in Australia starting in 1788 to relieve overcrowding in British prisons.

prompt: What flavor is 'Ube' ice cream, a wildly popular variety originally from the Philippines?
factBlurb: Ube is a purple yam native to the Philippines — its naturally vibrant violet color and sweet, nutty flavor have made ube ice cream a global sensation.

prompt: A traditional gondola in Venice is propelled by a gondolier using a single oar. What is the name of the distinctive oarlock that makes this possible?
factBlurb: The forcola is a hand-carved wooden oarlock unique to Venice — its complex curves let the gondolier pivot the oar into multiple rowing positions.

prompt: The Battle of Leyte Gulf in October 1944 is considered the largest naval battle in history. Where did it take place?
factBlurb: Fought October 23–26, 1944, Leyte Gulf involved over 200,000 personnel and effectively destroyed Japan's ability to conduct large naval operations.

prompt: In the card game War, what happens when both players flip a card of equal value — the 'war' condition?
options: The hand is replayed with one card each
Each player places three cards face-down, then flips one to battle
The tied cards are removed from the game
The player with the higher suit wins the tie
factBlurb: In classic War, a tie triggers 'war': each player deals three face-down cards, then flips a fourth — the higher flip wins all the cards on the table.

prompt: What color background does a U.S. SCHOOL ZONE warning sign use?
factBlurb: Since the 1990s, school zone signs switched from plain yellow to fluorescent yellow-green — studies showed it's the most visible color to the human eye in daylight.

prompt: Which ocean current brings cold water from the Antarctic to the coasts of South America, Africa, and Australia?
factBlurb: Also called the Peru Current, it's one of the most productive fishing regions on Earth due to nutrient-rich upwelling.

prompt: What amino acid found in high concentrations in watermelon is linked to improved athletic performance?
factBlurb: Watermelon is one of the richest natural sources of L-citrulline, which the body converts to arginine and may help reduce muscle soreness.

prompt: Bill Nye won a Steve Martin look-alike contest in which city?
factBlurb: Nye won a Steve Martin look-alike contest in Seattle — one of the quirky early career footnotes he's mentioned in interviews.

prompt: Which historic Madison brewery, founded in 1849, is the oldest continuously operating brewery in Wisconsin?
factBlurb: The Gipfel Brewery (also known as Gipfel's) has been brewing beer in Madison since 1849, longer than any other Wisconsin brewery.

prompt: Which tool company invented the oscillating multi-tool category with its Fein Multimaster in 1967?
factBlurb: Fein's Multimaster was the original oscillating tool, invented to remove plaster casts from patients — it took decades before competitors could legally copy the design after the patent expired.

prompt: Which artist released the album 'Jagged Little Pill' in 1995?
factBlurb: Alanis Morissette's 'Jagged Little Pill' became one of the best-selling debut albums ever, with 'You Oughta Know' as its breakthrough hit.

topic: Sports teams whose mascot is a bird
prompt: The Hawthorn Hawks play in which Australian professional league?
factBlurb: Hawthorn is one of the AFL's most successful teams, winning 13 premierships, with four consecutive titles from 2013-2015.

prompt: In what year was the very first Star Wars film released in theaters?
factBlurb: Released May 25, 1977, it was originally titled just 'Star Wars' before being retitled 'A New Hope' after the sequels became hits.
